name: Soft Saber Pelts

angles.text: As a tailor, you can turn saber pelts into sturdy, soft blankets and shawls for cold travel on the frontier.
As a hunter, you respect saber predators and hunt them when they threaten the roads.

faq.answer: Saber cats near the roads threaten travelers and merchants. Hunting them keeps the routes safer for those passing through.
faq.q: Why are travelers asked to hunt sabers?

faq.answer: Their thick fur makes durable, warm blankets and shawls that help guard against the weather.
faq.q: What are the saber pelts used for?

faq.answer: Local merchants and crafters trade with hunters for useful materials. For quality pelts, they offer sturdy, soft goods made through their craft.
faq.q: Who seeks to trade for these saber pelts?

faq.answer: Yes. Large saber cats hunt across wide territories that can overlap with frontier roads. Couriers and caravans risk sudden attacks where the cats roam.
faq.q: Do wild sabers pose a real threat to the roads?

faq.answer: The hunter receives a soft, durable keepsake in thanks for the pelts. It recalls the great cats hunted along the frontier.
faq.q: What is given in return for the pelts?

faq.answer: Traders may regret killing such regal creatures, but they see the hunt as necessary to protect travelers and make practical use of the warm pelts.
faq.q: How do local traders view the hunting of such majestic beasts?

sections.body: Saber cats prowl the roads used by couriers, merchants, and lone travelers across Azeroth. People may admire their grace, yet growing numbers near trade routes bring sudden attacks. Hunters keep those roads safe for everyone who depends on them.
sections.title: Securing the Wilderness Roads

sections.body: The hunt yields more than pelts. Frontier camps value saber cats’ dense coats for their warmth and strength. Skilled hands make the pelts into shawls and heavy blankets, giving shelter from harsh weather.
sections.title: Warmth from the Hunt

summary: Across Azeroth, Soft Saber Pelts come from cats that threaten travelers on the roads. Their thick coats make warm blankets and shawls.
